headline: 30 trades, net -1.04 bps/bet (total -31.3); rolling 16-bet gross ~flat at -0.97 bps. Signal flat at 0.
regime_note: BTC ~$83.5k, consolidating well above the low-$63k mid-August prints after the late-August step-up; choppy, high-vol tape. Signal is 0, so no live position right now.
assessment_md:
**How it's doing.** Essentially unchanged from last check. The strategy has logged 30 resolved trades, averaging **-1.04 bps per bet** (cumulative -31.3 bps), with a 40% win rate. The rolling 16-bet window shows **gross -0.97 bps** before costs and **-3.97 bps** net at an assumed 3 bps cost. No new trade appears to have resolved since the prior update, and the live signal is **0** (no position).

**What changed.** Nothing material — numbers match the prior assessment. BTC sits near $83.5k, consolidating after the big late-August jump from the low-$60ks.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us.** This is a small, slow-growing sample by design (only ~1-2% of candles trade). Thirty trades cannot confirm or reject a ~4 bps edge: the per-trade results swing wildly (from +49 bps to -28 bps), so the mean is dominated by a handful of outliers and is statistically noisy. A slightly negative gross over 30 bets is **consistent with both a dead edge and a real-but-marginal one** — we genuinely can't distinguish yet. Note the backtested edge was already marginal (~4 bps gross vs ~3.9 bps breakeven), and the independent edge search found **0 survivors** that clear net-positive on both venues at 5 bps cost.

**Bottom line.** Too thin to judge, and the prior evidence says this is marginal at best — likely not net-profitable after realistic costs. No degradation alert warranted, but no sign of a reliable edge either. Keep collecting data; don't expect profit.
